# LibreSesh

> A scheduling tool for conferences and unconferences: one server, one SQLite
> file, a schedule a room full of people can edit together. This instance hosts
> one or more events, each at `/e/<slug>`, each behind its own password. There
> is no public view of any event, no accounts, and nothing to buy.

An event has rooms, a programme of sessions across days, a board of pitched
sessions people register interest in, and notes, links and questions attached
to each session. Everything updates live over Server-Sent Events.

If you are a program acting for someone here, start with
[/agents.md](/agents.md) — how to get in, what you may do, and what not to do
on a person's behalf. It is the canonical description of this instance for
agents; this file is the short version of it.

## Docs

- [/agents.md](/agents.md): the operating manual — access, the four-step flow,
  the limits, the policy on acting for a human.
- [/SKILL.md](/SKILL.md): the same capabilities packaged as a skill, if your
  harness consumes that format.
- [/api.md](/api.md): the full HTTP reference — every endpoint, every error
  code, the rate limits.
- [/api/events](/api/events): the only unauthenticated endpoint. Names and
  dates of the events on this instance; no schedule content.

## Three things that will save you the trouble

- **One request gets a whole schedule.** `GET /api/e/<slug>/bundle` returns the
  entire event. Nothing to crawl, no pagination.
- **Subscribe rather than poll.** `GET /api/e/<slug>/stream` carries every
  change and is not rate limited.
- **Keep your cookie jar.** Identity is a signed cookie; there is no bearer
  token. A client that drops it gets `401` on everything.

## Source

[github.com/marceljay/libresesh](https://github.com/marceljay/libresesh) — the
server, the web app, and the architecture and security notes behind both.
